symptoms.heading: Is your pump experiencing any of these problems?
symptoms.sub: Running a pump with damaged bearings or low insulation burns out the motor coil. Call us early to prevent severe motor damage.
symptoms.item1Desc: Worn out impellers, choked suction strainer, or broken shaft coupling drop water pressure.
symptoms.item2Desc: High current draw, grounded stator winding, or weak starting capacitor cause tripping.
symptoms.item3Desc: Sand jamming impellers, open phase wire, or seized bush bearings freeze the motor.
symptoms.item4Desc: Bent rotor shaft, worn thrust bearing, or misaligned column pipe create intense vibration.

process.heading: Our 4-Step Repair Procedure
process.sub: From initial testing to final water pressure bench testing, here is how we ensure reliable operation.
process.step1Desc: We test winding continuity, megger insulation resistance, and rotor shaft rotation.
process.step2Desc: Pump stages, impellers, thrust bearing, rotor shaft, and stator coils are inspected.
process.step3Desc: Motor coils are rewound with pure copper; impellers and mechanical seals are replaced.
process.step4Desc: Waterproof chamber seals are re-pressurized. Full electrical current and discharge testing.

troubleshooting.heading: Common Pump Problems & Self-Check Solutions
troubleshooting.sub: Before calling a technician or pulling a pump from the borewell, check these basic electrical and mechanical points yourself. Often a simple switch or capacitor is all that is needed.
troubleshooting.note: Always turn off the main switch/MCB before inspecting control panel terminals or wiring. Never touch electrical connections with wet hands.
troubleshooting.searchPlaceholder: Search pump symptoms or problems (e.g. starter trip, no water, humming)...

issues.title: 1. Starter Not Turning On / Motor Not Starting At All
issues.symptoms: Pressing the green starter button produces no response, or contactor will not engage.
selfCheck: Check if main breaker (MCB) or fuse has tripped.
Check voltage tester on input lines to confirm full 3-phase power (or 220V on single-phase).
Press the red overload reset button on the starter relay.
issues.solution: If voltage is below 180V or one phase is missing, do not attempt to start. Once voltage stabilizes, press the reset button and restart.

issues.title: 2. Starter Engages But Trips Out Within 5 to 10 Seconds
issues.symptoms: Motor tries to turn and the starter contactor abruptly cuts off.
selfCheck: Observe the starter ammeter: is the needle jumping past normal current into high overload?
On single-phase motors, check if the run/start capacitor is bulged or weak.
Verify the discharge water delivery valve is not fully shut or blocked.
issues.solution: Replace bulged or weak capacitors with identical MFD rating. If amp draw exceeds 30-40A, the pump may be mechanically seized; do not repeatedly restart to protect the windings.

issues.title: 3. Motor Running Smoothly But Delivering Zero Water
issues.symptoms: Starter remains on, motor sound is audible, but no water reaches the discharge pipe.
selfCheck: On 3-phase pumps, check if the motor is rotating backward (reversed phase rotation).
Has the underground borewell water table dropped below the pump intake?
Is the column pipe check valve (NRV) stuck shut?
issues.solution: On 3-phase starters, swap any two incoming phase wires (e.g., Red and Blue). This reverses motor rotation to forward, instantly restoring discharge. If still dry, water level may be depleted.

issues.title: 4. Low Water Discharge Pressure or Surging with Air Bubbles
issues.symptoms: Water flow is cut in half or surges irregularly with spurts of air.
selfCheck: Inspect surface pipes, elbows, and nipples for pinhole leaks or cracked fittings.
Check if water discharge contains heavy silt or sand.
Check line voltage: low voltage reduces motor RPM and discharge head.
issues.solution: If voltage is nominal, column pipes down the well may have cracked or impellers have eroded from abrasive sand. An overhaul is required to replace worn diffusers.

issues.title: 5. Starter Produces Loud Buzzing/Humming, Motor Doesn't Spin
issues.symptoms: Motor fails to spin, a loud hum comes from the starter or motor, and wires heat up rapidly.
selfCheck: Check for Single Phasing (loss of one phase in a 3-phase supply).
On single-phase motors, verify the start capacitor terminal wire has not disconnected.
issues.solution: Immediately push the red Stop button! Single phasing will incinerate copper stator coils within 60 seconds. Rectify utility line power before restarting.
